stem:
[Image: A graph of soft drink sales for cherry cola and lemon cola by year and number of cans in millions.]

The graph shows the sales of two types of soft drink over 4 years. If the sales trends continue for the next 10 years, determine the year in which the sales of Cherry Cola will be the same as the sales of Lemon Cola.
figure_description:
A vertical bar graph titled "Soft Drink Sales".
The vertical axis is labeled "Number of cans\n(millions)" with grid marks and horizontal lines at intervals of 10 from 0 to 60.
The horizontal axis is labeled "Year" with four years: 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001.
A legend shows:
- White box: Cherry Cola
- Solid black box: Lemon Cola

For each year, there is a pair of adjacent bars (Cherry Cola on the left, Lemon Cola on the right):
- 1998: Cherry Cola bar reaches 10; Lemon Cola bar reaches 40.
- 1999: Cherry Cola bar reaches 20; Lemon Cola bar reaches 45.
- 2000: Cherry Cola bar reaches 30; Lemon Cola bar reaches 50.
- 2001: Cherry Cola bar reaches 40; Lemon Cola bar reaches 55.
